findings.location: Definition, opening paragraph: “every compact time-state cylinder C⊂D”
findings.evidence: The definition does not specify the shape or quantification of a “compact time-state cylinder,” although this determines which pairs (t,x),(t,y) must share one Lipschitz constant. If it means an arbitrary compact set, a two-point set makes the condition vacuous for each pair; a product time interval and state ball imposes a nontrivial uniform bound. The cited ODE-domain definition supplies no cylinder convention. Specify the sets and quantifiers, or state an explicit local Lipschitz condition near every point.

findings.location: Proof 1.1, sentence claiming local existence around every graph point makes the union domain open
findings.evidence: Local existence at a graph point produces a solution through that point, but does not by itself put it in the family of solutions through the original initial datum whose domains are being unioned. Apply the cited overlap/gluing lemma to join it to a representative through the original datum before concluding the union domain is open. This is a short omitted step.

findings.location: Proof 2.1, sentence inferring bijectivity from a trivial kernel
findings.evidence: From Mv=0 implying v=0, the proof concludes that M is bijective but cites only def-invertible-matrix-and-general-linear-group, which defines invertibility but does not prove injective implies surjective in finite dimension. The proof also writes (M^{1/2})^{-1} without establishing surjectivity of M^{1/2}; positivity only gives trivial kernel. Add the finite-dimensional injective-implies-surjective theorem (for example thm-invertible-matrix-theorem) or prove it locally.

findings.location: Statement, first sentence defining q as a C² curve on an arbitrary interval I
findings.evidence: On first review, the statement used C² for q:I→Rⁿ when I could be a singleton or nonopen interval, while the cited C² definition applies to maps on open Euclidean domains. The current source has since been changed to require an order-convex domain with at least two points and explicit continuous domain-relative derivatives, which closes this defect. The earlier bytes were not hash-bound before that edit; this is a historical finding, not a claim about current bytes.
